about: The round 2 progress page's own words and the files each section reads. work/build/scripts/phase-3/progress_round_2_build.py reads this file on every run; every number and picture on the page comes from the files named under slots, read at build time. A {name} in a sentence is filled from those files. Codes in a 'refs' field print only in the small reference lines. The rule numbers under carried, sections.entry.rule and sections.changed.charts only choose what the page shows, as the brief names it; the build reads every fact about them from their files.
title: Edition 06 Round 2 Progress

cover.title: Round 2, as it stands
cover.deck_rescored: Round 2 drew {n_fam_w} more families of charts for chapter 14, set each of their forms in as an entry, and built {n15_w} more rules for chapter 15. This page shows that work after the review, the fix pass and the creative director’s second scores.
cover.deck_building: Round 2 drew {n_fam_w} more families of charts for chapter 14, set each of their forms in as an entry, and built {n15_w} more rules for chapter 15. This page shows that work as it stands while the fix pass runs. It fills in again once the creative director’s second scores land.
cover.no_decision: This page asks you nothing. Board 2 follows round 3, and that is where you decide.
cover.minutes: Pictures show at true size. Where one is wider than your window, its frame scrolls sideways.

carried.interval: Its correct plate is now drawn by the chart kit’s {form}, the form of Rule {form_rule}.
carried.point: Its correct plate puts the view’s one red on the line for {name}
carried.style: Printed once for every rule plate, in one shared block of {b} bytes. The rules for every chart, with the opener, weigh {ro} bytes against their allowance of {al}.
carried.ch13_all: All {n} of its chart titles now end with a period.
carried.ch13_some: {k} of its {n} chart titles end with a period.
carried.wide: At a {w1} px and a {w2} px window, {k} of the chapter’s wide plates draw their full {px} px stage.
carried.not_found: Not shown done in its files at this build.

charts.title: The {n_new} new charts
charts.lede: Each chart as the chart kit draws it, from the kit’s own pictures. The first pair is on Newsprint and the second on Charcoal; in each, the drawing for a 1440 px page sits beside the drawing for a 390 px phone page. The line under each pair gives the chart’s size in the guide and the result of the kit’s own check.
charts.lede_mark: {n_marked_cap} of them, {marked_ids}, draw a publisher’s modeled or projected figures. The guide labels each one “{mark_label}” beside the publisher’s product, and their headers below carry the same label.

changed.title: Two round 1 charts the round changed
changed.lede: Round 2’s rulings on how a chart marks what its title names reached two charts from round 1. Each is shown as the new charts are, with a line on what changed.

charts.what: What changed: the two fifths its title names, the highest and the lowest, now take the subject ink with no red, and the middle three stay light with their values printed.
What changed: the all receipts line is dashed in the text’s ink, the one treatment every total or national line now takes.

entry.title: How an entry reads in the guide
entry.lede: Every form in chapter 14 gets one numbered entry in the same order: the rule, when to use the form, what to use instead, why it works, then its example chart with the chart’s table. Here is Rule {entry_rule}, “{entry_title}”, photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window and at a 390 px window.
entry.phone_line: Where a chart draws a different form on a phone, the entry sets the phone drawing beside the desk one. This one is headed “{entry_phone}”.

sketches.title: The {n_sketch_w} sketches
sketches.lede: Round 2 gives {n_sketch_w} forms a small sketch with invented, labeled data in place of a finished chart: {n_avoid_w} the guide tells builders to avoid, each drawn beside the better choice, and {n_ref_w} it keeps for reference. Each is photographed at a 1440 px window, with its heading and caption printed under it as the guide prints them. The forms to avoid come first.
sketches.h_avoid: Forms to avoid, each beside the better choice

rules.title: The rules for every chart, as round 2 changed them
rules.lede: Round 2 changed {n_changed_w} of the rules that hold for every chart: {changed_list}. Each rule has two plates, the framed examples under it: a correct one and a failure. Both are photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window, one above the other where they do not fit side by side. The chapter’s opening plate comes first.

ch15.title: Chapter 15’s {n15_w} new rules
ch15.lede: Round 2 built {n15_w} more of chapter 15’s rules, {n15_plates} plates in all. Each plate is photographed from today’s guide at a 1440 px window and at a 390 px window, side by side. Rule {wide_rule}’s {wide_kind} also shows at a 1024 px window, where the chapter’s wide stage now holds.
ch15.wide_h: The same plate at a 1024 px window
ch15.wide_cap: At a 1024 px window the plate keeps its {wide_px} px stage.

scores.title: Scores
scores.cd_lede: The creative director scores {cd_items_w} parts of round 2 from 1 to 5 on {cd_crit_w} counts: {cd_crit}. A part ships at 4 or more on every count.
scores.cd_lede_wait: The creative director scores each part of round 2 from 1 to 5 on each count of the studio’s rubric. A part ships at 4 or more on every count.
scores.legend_first: Each cell shows the first score. A cell with a frame is under 4.
scores.legend_both: Each cell shows the first score in small type, then the second score after the fix pass. A shaded cell moved. A cell with a frame is under 4.
scores.cd_wait: The creative director’s first scores join this table when their file lands.
scores.cd_re_wait: The second scores, after the fix pass, join this table when their file lands; each cell then shows both.
scores.none_ready: The first scores find none of the {n} parts ready yet: each has a score under 4 or a Must fix open.
scores.rt_lede: {n_rt_cap} reviewers read round 2 beside the creative director, each from one side. Each gave a score from 1 to 5 and numbered what it found. After the fix pass, each reads its own findings again and gives a second score.
scores.rt_note: Must fix means a fault that breaks a rule, misleads or blocks a task. Should fix means a fault that weakens the work. Each count is read from the report’s own numbered findings, and the second score from its section on the second pass.

weight.title: Weight
weight.lede: The guide is one file, so every chart adds to what a reader downloads. These figures come from the build report of today’s strict build.
weight.fig_caption: Each bar shows how much of its limit a part uses today.

weight.per_plate: Chapter 14 weighs {ch14_bytes} bytes against its stop of {ch14_stop} bytes. That leaves {per_plate} bytes for each of the {plates_to_come} finished charts still to come, after the room the kit and the chapter’s other parts still need.
weight.ch15_line: Chapter 15 weighs {ch15_bytes} bytes against its ceiling of {ch15_ceiling}.
weight.page_line: The guide weighs {page_bytes} bytes today. With every chapter still to come counted at its full allocation, it projects to {proj_bytes} bytes, {proj_room} bytes under the {budget_mb} MB the page may reach.
